<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- A `harness hooks` verb family that is BOTH the management surface (install/status/uninstall/list) and the runtime the installed hooks invoke (fire) — the config we write points back at harness, so upgrading harness upgrades hook behaviour with no reinstall.
- Hooks installed into every agent client harness supports, driven by ONE declarative matrix rather than per-client bespoke code.
- A git intercept that detects a genuine new commit and never guesses — a missing note is recoverable, a false one is a confident wrong answer nobody audits.
- A trace2 tickler that restores attribution under a sandbox with ZERO changes to the customer machine — no trace2 redirection, no sandbox setting, no security trade.
- Doctor installs hooks alongside the pinned git-ai, under the existing safeLayer containment and warn-only exit-0 posture.
- Hook actions pluggable, so commit detection is the first action and not the only one.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Fixing the human-absorption case (human lines stamped AI). It was never reproduced here — everything reproduced was TOTAL LOSS — and it is a different defect. Do not describe this plan as fixing it.
- Explaining or fixing Claude Code Bash-class tool calls recording nothing on an unsandboxed machine (dossier 7.5). Unexplained, separate, and possibly the real cause of the original complaint.
- Changing customer machine configuration — no global trace2 redirection, no Cursor sandbox edits, no writes to ~/.cursor beyond the hook entry we own.
- Filing issues upstream to git-ai.
- Proving Windows end to end. The named-pipe path is code-portable but unobserved, and verification needs the remote Windows agent.

<a id="research-context"></a>

## Research Context

Measured 2026-08-09. Evidence: assets/research-dossier.md (the failure chain, the controlled A/B, five measured dead ends), assets/workshops/hooks-installing.md (the authoritative installer design, from a full read of git-ai's 15 installers), assets/poc/ (16 working artifacts). Controlled A/B in a real sandboxed Cursor session: hook DISABLED produced NO note on a four-file mixed commit; hook ENABLED produced a correct three-way split (cursor / human / claude), with the human's 11 hand-written lines correctly separated. The git-ai install and parse surfaces are byte-identical between our v1.6.21 pin and the v1.6.22 checkout (verified by diff over src/mdm, install_hooks.rs and checkpoint_agent/), so the installer reference applies to the pin with no version caveat.

<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

Cursor's sandbox refuses AF_UNIX connect(), so a sandboxed `git commit` never reaches the git-ai daemon and NO note is written at all — total attribution loss, not misattribution. The hook runner is not sandboxed. This plan makes harness own agent-harness hooks end to end: a `harness hooks` verb family that is BOTH the installer and the runtime the installed hooks call back into, a git intercept that detects a real new commit from HEAD, and a trace2 tickler that tells the daemon a commit happened so it writes the note it would otherwise miss. Nothing on the customer machine changes — no trace2 redirection, no sandbox setting, no security trade.

<a id="testing-strategy"></a>

## Testing Strategy

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| approach | Hybrid — real behaviour against a live git-ai daemon for the intercept and the tickler; table-driven fixture tests for the agent matrix and the installer. |
| rationale | The tickler cannot be proven by a fake: the finding IS that the daemon accepts a synthesised stream, so a fake that accepts it proves nothing. The installer is pure file transformation and needs no live anything. |
| focus_areas | Commit-detection edge cases (the dangerous direction); config merge preserving foreign entries byte-identically; comment and key-order preservation; install/uninstall symmetry; idempotency; exit-0 on every failure path; a binary path containing spaces. |
| excluded | Windows end-to-end (no instrument until the remote agent reports); git-ai internals we do not own; Codex TOML trust state (deferred). |
| mock_usage | Targeted only — fake adapters for the fs, git and socket ports per the constitution (fakes over mocks; never vi.mock of internal modules). |

<a id="implementation-summary"></a>

## Implementation Summary

Three phases. Phase 1 builds the runtime that is already proven — `harness hooks fire`, the HEAD-parent commit intercept, and the six-event trace2 tickler — behind ports, with the dangerous false-positive cases attacked rather than merely tested. Phase 2 builds the installer from ONE declarative matrix over four write strategies (JSON merge, plugin file, script file, and TOML deferred), fixing the four things git-ai gets wrong: no backups, order-and-comment-destroying writes, a two-substring ownership test, and unquoted paths. Phase 3 wires it into doctor beside the pinned git-ai install and documents it. Codex (TOML + sha256 trust state) and the three IDE-level targets are explicitly out of the matrix.

<a id="key-findings"></a>

## Key Findings

| impact | finding | action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | Cursor's sandbox refuses AF_UNIX connect() — EPERM on BOTH git-ai daemon sockets — so a sandboxed git commit never reaches the daemon and NO note is written at all. Not misattribution: total loss, including AI lines that were checkpointed correctly. | The defect the plan exists to fix. Reproduce it in CI without Cursor via GIT_TRACE2_EVENT pointed at a discarded path. |
| Critical | The daemon control API has no 'a commit happened' request (verified at the v1.6.21 pin: ping, checkpoint.run, sync.family, status.family, telemetry.submit, cas.submit, notes.flush, snapshot.watermarks, bash_session.*, bash_hook_attempt.*, await, shutdown). trace2 is the ONLY ingress to the note writer. | The fix must speak trace2. Do not look for a politer API — it does not exist. |
| Critical | A real git commit trace2 stream carries NO sha; the daemon resolves the transition from a reflog cursor it already holds (ingestion spec ownership rule 1). It does not need the real stream — only to be told a commit command ran in repo X. | Six synthetic events suffice. Proven three times, including a controlled A/B. |
| High | The hook runner is NOT sandboxed (CURSOR_SANDBOX unset, both sockets reachable) while the agent shell is. The entire design rests on this, and it is measured on macOS only. | Verify on Linux in Phase 1 and hand Windows to the remote agent. Treat as an assumption until measured, never as a fact. |
| High | git-ai takes NO backups anywhere (exhaustive grep, zero matches) and only ONE of its fifteen writers preserves comments. serde_json is declared without preserve_order, so every install alphabetically re-sorts the user's whole settings file. | Back up before first write; use comment- and order-preserving writes everywhere. This is the main thing we do differently. |
| High | git-ai's ownership predicate is cmd.contains('git-ai') && cmd.contains('checkpoint'), used bare by four installers — so uninstall silently deletes any user hook whose command mentions both words. | Match on an explicit marker we own. Never a substring heuristic over someone else's command. |
| High | Emitting a commit event when no commit happened could make the daemon claim an unrelated reflog entry — a FALSE note, worse than a missing one. | Detect by HEAD-parent equality, never by matching text in the command. Attack this case deliberately. |
| Medium | Seven git-ai installers interpolate an UNQUOTED binary path into a shell string, and only three call normalize_windows_path_for_shell. A path containing a space produces a broken hook. | Always quote and always normalise, for every agent. |
| Medium | Three git-ai installers (amp, opencode, pi) test a RELATIVE marker path, making detection cwd-dependent. | Absolute markers only, and status reports evidence rather than belief. |
| Medium | Agents write compound && chains unprompted, which defeats Cursor terminal allowlisting — git was already allowlisted and the commit still ran sandboxed. | Never rely on or recommend an allowlist as a remedy. |

<a id="risks"></a>

## Risks

| risk | likelihood | impact | mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A wrong emit makes the daemon attribute an unrelated reflog entry, producing a confident false note. | Medium | Critical | HEAD-parent guard; deliberate provocation tests (checkout, reset, rebase, amend, double-commit, no-op); stay silent whenever the transition is not exactly one new commit. |
| The hook runner is sandboxed on Windows or Linux, invalidating the mechanism there. | Medium | Critical | Measure on Linux in Phase 1. Ship Windows as UNVERIFIED rather than assumed; the remote agent is the only instrument. |
| Writing into a shared agent config destroys another tool's entries, or silently re-sorts and de-comments the user's file. | High | High | Comment- and order-preserving writes; back up before first write; fixture tests that install with git-ai's own entries present and assert they survive byte-identical. |
| Our uninstall leaves debris, as every git-ai uninstall does. | High | Medium | Uninstall symmetry is a test: install then uninstall must return the file to its ORIGINAL bytes. |
| git-ai changes the socket path, the pipe-name digest, or the trace2 event shape in a later version. | Medium | High | Pin, and carry one MEASURED_AGAINST_PIN constant whose drift from the live version is reported at runtime rather than failing silently. |
| Node process startup on every tool call adds latency (two invocations per tool use). | Medium | Low | Exit before loading anything on tool names that cannot be commit-bearing. Watch-item, not a gate — harness already runs many times a session. |
| An absolute binary path in the customer config breaks when npm relocates the binary on upgrade. | Medium | Medium | Follow git-ai (decided). harness hooks status detects a path that no longer resolves; doctor reports it. |

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Never emit a synthetic commit event unless HEAD advanced by exactly one commit whose first parent is the previously recorded HEAD. When in doubt, stay silent — a missing note is recoverable, a false one is not.
- Every hook code path exits 0 and writes nothing the agent can see. A broken harness must never break the customer's editor session. This is a DELIBERATE deviation from the exit-code anti-pattern (gate G2) and failures must surface through `harness hooks status` instead.
- Back up any config file before our first write to it, and name the backup in the output. git-ai takes none; that is the gap we are closing.
- Preserve comments and key order in every file we touch. Never re-serialize a user's config wholesale.
- Match only on a marker we own. Never claim or delete a hook entry using a substring heuristic over someone else's command.
- Refuse to overwrite an unmanaged file rather than clobbering it (git-ai's Cline installer is the model; its Amp installer is the counter-example).
- Assert on note IDENTITY per commit, never on a note COUNT — the count moves for unrelated reasons.
- Measure behaviour against the PINNED git-ai version, never the ~/github/git-ai checkout HEAD.
- Do not retry the five measured dead ends in dossier section 6.
- Never recommend that a customer weaken their sandbox; networkPolicy default allow opens ALL egress and is not a remedy we ship.
